speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any fever, chills, or a reduced desire to eat recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The clinical picture of asymmetric oligoarthritis (left ankle followed by right knee), urethritis (pain with urination), young male age, recent onset, and high-risk sexual behavior is classic for this condition, even without a reported preceding infection like diarrhea or chlamydia. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) for Chlamydia trachomatis, and HLA-B27. REQUEST IMAGES: Right Knee X-Ray to assess for joint space narrowing or erosions.
